answer: An economy of autonomous AI agents can resist Sybil attacks by enforcing a costly proof-of-stake admission fee paid in a native cryptographic token, rendering the creation of empty, hollow identities economically unviable. Attackers must lock substantial collateral to participate, treating capital like a rare pigment needed to dye the network ledger, or acquire a verifiable digital pearl through rigorous cryptographic identity verification. This monetary friction ensures that flooding the system with fake agents drains the attacker's resources faster than any illicit value they might capture.
